subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module with the SDK, thinking through realistic phoenix proportions—roughly a 2.4 meter wingspan and 1.2 meter body—and considering how to position the model mid-flight, elevated off the ground to convey a rising pose.

I'm also reviewing the builder API I'll rely on: creating a builder with name and detail options, then using its joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, spike, rod, capsule, ring, and surface methods, along with color/paint utilities like gradient and mottle, to keep the construction accurate and avoid misusing the interface.

Now I'm sketching the phoenix skeleton itself: hips placed as the root at a hovering height, with the spine running horizontally from tail base to chest and the head extending forward and slightly upward, using a catmull spline through a handful of points to define the body's curve.

Now I'm planning the head and jaw joints, then setting up the wing chains as shoulder-to-wrist-to-tip limbs spread open and outward for the flying pose.

Confirmed, names count matches points count for tipped chains. Now I'm figuring out how to build the wing feathers: fanning primary feathers from the wing tip using flat extruded plates with a crimson-to-gold gradient, tapering their shape and positioning each along the wing chain.

Defining feather geometry...

Defining color bands/paint logic...

For the tail, I'm planning long tapered sweeps painted like ribbons of fire. For the crest, I'm working out how to place a ring of flame-shaped plumes around the head using a ring callback that generates bezier sweeps for each spike, figuring out how to position the control points for each item's frame.

For eyes, I'll use gold-painted spheres with small dark pupils since true emissive isn't an option. For the beak, I'm planning separate upper and lower sweeps forming a hooked golden shape joined at a jaw bone, and I'll scatter small glowing spheres as embers and sparks along the wings.

I need to stay within the 1000-part limit, so I'm budgeting roughly 24 primary feathers plus secondaries and 7 tail feathers per side. For symmetry, I'll mirror wing and limb positions by flipping the x-coordinate for left versus right, keeping joint names suffixed uniquely per side, and I'm laying out approximate coordinates for a 2.6m wingspan with the body centered at x=0 facing +Z, making sure the tail ribbons stay comfortably above ground level.

Building out the skeletal chain now... hips joint, then a spine catmull chain from lower back up through the shoulders, followed by a neck chain and head joint anchored to the last neck segment, with a jaw joint parented off the head using local offset coordinates.

For the jaw, I'm working through the beak geometry next, defining an upper beak sweep that curves forward and hooks downward at the tip using local coordinates relative to the head's orientation.

I'm sketching the lower mandible as a small bezier sweep off the jaw joint, explicitly passing the jaw bone so the mesh binds correctly. For the eyes, I'm working out the side convention for head.local coordinates, since the docs define s=1 as the right side even though that maps to +X locally, which is the opposite of world space.

For the skull, I'm considering a capsule shape anchored at the head joint rather than a plain sphere to get a more elongated form, binding it to the head bone with a crimson color. I'm also planning to use position-based paint gradients so the body transitions from crimson near the torso to gold at the extremities.

For wings, I'm setting up each feather as a sweep from root to tip, mapping a color gradient along the sweep parameter so feathers shift from crimson at the base to gold at the tip, consistent with the rest of the body gradient. I'm also laying out the wing skeleton joints—shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip—mirrored symmetrically across the X axis to define the wing's pose.

Still placing feathers along the wing chain...

Computing offset points...

Still defining feather points...

Now I'm shaping the tail chain, curving back and down from the pelvis through several named points to form the trailing feathers.

Still writing tail geometry...

Adding flame plume spikes...

Working out spike geometry with bezier curves for each crest flame, offsetting x per spike for variety and tapering the sweep radius to a point at the tip.

Now I'm adding glowing amber eyes with bright pupils, then scattering small ember spheres along the wings using a seeded RNG for deterministic gold, orange, and yellow particles positioned with randomized spread.

I'll keep the palette to around 8 shared colors since standard materials can't emit light anyway, so no glow needed. For embers, I'll add small drifting spheres near the wing tips as simple trail accents rather than complex sweeps.

Now I'm deciding whether to add tucked legs for the flight pose—simple golden sweep curves running from hip to ankle should work well enough without overcomplicating the budget.

With naming sorted, I'm shifting to the torso sweep: using a radius function along the spine chain that's slimmer at the tail, fuller through the chest, and tapering near the shoulders, painted in the body color.

Then I'm applying a similar tapering sweep to the neck and head, and finally doing the wing arm tubes with gradient paints from crimson to orange, letting the chain-based skinning naturally bend the mesh with the skeleton.

Setting up the color palette with crimson, gold, amber and dark tones for the beak and eye, plus a flame gradient helper that blends colors smoothly along a parameter.

Writing feather color logic...

Now I'm thinking about wing shape and feather placement: primaries fanning from the hand along the wing's chain path, with smaller covert feathers near the arm root using shorter lengths. I'm starting to write a general feather helper function that takes the wing, position, spread, length, and color to draw each feather consistently.

Writing feather curve code...

Now I'm thinking about tail ribbons, planning to derive them from the tail chain's points with a parameter spanning across the tail width for a fanned effect.

For each ribbon I'm setting a start and end offset, curving a bezier path that trails downward and back, then sweeping a tapered radius along it with a flame-like crimson-to-gold gradient. I'll sweep the main tail bone with a thicker crimson radius, and then move on to designing the crest as seven plumes atop the head using a similar bezier approach.

Now I'm placing the beak as an upper bezier sweep rooted at the front of the head sphere, tapering outward with a gold color, making sure the root position sits forward of the head joint to match the head capsule's radius.

Next I'm setting up a jaw joint parented to the head, oriented forward using an aim target, so the lower beak can hinge from roughly the same origin point.

Then I'm sculpting the lower mandible as a bezier sweep from the jaw outward with tapering radius and a dark gold color, matching the upper beak's shape so they meet as a closed beak. After that I start adding spherical eyes positioned symmetrically on each side of the head.

Still shaping legs and talons...

Now I'm setting up the wing chains, parenting them to the spine and placing shoulder joints symmetrically. I'm looping over left and right sides to build feather fans—primaries along the wing edge and coverts closer to the arm—sweeping outward and back for a dramatic flung-open look.

I'm sizing the feather lengths so the tips reach a reasonable wingspan without the fan becoming oversized, then working out the bezier control points for each feather's curve outward from the root.

Writing feather geometry...

I'm adding glowing ember spheres in gold, orange, and yellow tones, then tallying up the total part count across wings, feathers, embers, and ribbons to keep things reasonable. Now I'm setting up the random number generator and importing the gradient and mix helpers needed for the paint functions.

Writing phoenix module setup...

Building the skeleton rig...

Still adjusting joint positions...

Continuing the chain down through neck joints, then the head joint aimed slightly forward and up, and the jaw joint—though I notice the jaw is placed coincident with the head position, creating a zero-length bone, which I should reconsider positioning slightly offset to avoid.

Now I'm building the wing chains for both left and right sides, creating a curved path through shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand-tip joints, then verifying the names-to-points counting matches the convention used elsewhere. I'm adding a sweep profile along the wing to give it thickness and color.

Now I'm writing a quill/feather function that samples a point along the wing chain at parameter t, then builds a bezier curve extending outward and backward from that point to form individual feather shapes, swept with a tapering radius based on feather length. I'm looping this function across indices to lay out primary and secondary feathers with varying positions, lengths, and droop.

I'm checking that the sweep radii and drop parameters look reasonable, then planning to add spark/ember details, tail ribbons, and finally the crest, beak, and eyes using local coordinates on the head joint, while trimming down unused imports to just the essentials I actually use.

Now I'm working out the tail ribbon geometry, computing bezier control points that fan outward from the tail's midpoint using a side offset, and sanity-checking the resulting ribbon lengths against the tail's position so they don't end up disproportionately long.

For the ribbon coloring I'm setting up a paint function that blends orange into gold toward the tips, with the base staying closer to crimson-orange, and applying a shrinking radius along the tail sweep.

Now I'm writing the crest plume geometry, looping through several feathers and computing bezier curves from base to tip using the head's local coordinate space with varying offsets and tapering radii.

I'm also working out the head orientation math to confirm it aims mostly forward with a slight upward tilt, placing the eyes relative to the head's local frame, and defining the body as a tapered sweep along the spine with sinusoidal thickness, followed by the neck and head capsule geometry.

Now I'm sketching the leg and talon construction using curved sweeps from the hips down to clawed spikes, then setting up an ember particle system that scatters glowing sparks behind the wings with randomized position, size, and color drawn from a gold/ember palette.

I should double-check that the hips joint is the true root with no parent, since every other chain branches from it, then wrap things up with a minimal explanation outside the code block.
